## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). See Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ When `execute_code` is available, use it to read Datadog data, even for a single lookup: one script can make several API calls, join data across products, and return only what the answer needs. Skill guides still apply for domain knowledge (query syntax, attribute and metric names, pitfalls), but where a guide tells you to call a specific read tool such as `search_datadog_logs`, `analyze_datadog_logs`, or `get_datadog_metric`, make the equivalent call from `execute_code` instead, using `search_datadog_sdk` to find it. This takes precedence over tool choices in skill guides. Use the named tool only when `search_datadog_sdk` finds no operation for what you need, or when `execute_code` still fails for a step after following its own error guidance. This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, entire/trails before trail work, entire/querying for the full querying reference. Load them proactively, at the start of the work, not after an error.

Feedback: if a tool is wrong, misleading, or missing something, call send_entire_feedback (name the tool). Code search is gated per jurisdiction — where the index is not deployed, those tools say so.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Select the Go packages a change set can affect, for PR test selection.
3	
4	Reads the changed file list (from git or --changed-files), maps every changed
5	.go file to its package, expands through the reverse import graph (production,
6	test, and external-test imports), and prints a JSON decision:
7	
8	  {"mode": "full"}                     — fall back to the complete suite
9	  {"mode": "none"}                     — no Go package is affected
10	  {"mode": "selected", "packages": []} — run exactly these packages
11	
12	The selection FAILS SAFE: any changed file that is not a .go file inside a
13	listed package directory — workflow edits, go.mod/go.sum, tools, embedded
14	assets, testdata — selects the full suite, because those inputs can change Go
15	behavior without changing a .go file. Selection must only ever narrow a run it
16	can prove is equivalent for the affected packages.
17	"""
18	import argparse
19	import json
20	import pathlib
21	import subprocess
22	import sys
23	
24	ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
25	
26	
27	def changed_files(base, head, cwd=ROOT):
28	    # --no-renames keeps a rename visible as an add plus a delete, so a .go
29	    # file moved between packages marks BOTH packages as changed. With rename
30	    # detection, --name-only lists only the destination and the source package
31	    # would silently keep its stale selection.
32	    output = subprocess.check_output(
33	        ["git", "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", f"{base}", f"{head}"],
34	        cwd=cwd,
35	        text=True,
36	    )
37	    return [line for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]
38	
39	
40	def load_packages(go):
41	    """Return {import_path: {dir, deps_on}} with reverse edges unexpanded."""
42	    output = subprocess.check_output(
43	        [go, "list", "-json=ImportPath,Dir,Imports,TestImports,XTestImports", "./..."],
44	        cwd=ROOT,
45	        text=True,
46	    )
47	    packages = {}
48	    decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
49	    index = 0
50	    while index < len(output):
51	        while index < len(output) and output[index] in " \r\n\t":
52	            index += 1
53	        if index >= len(output):
54	            break
55	        package, end = decoder.raw_decode(output, index)
56	        index = end
57	        packages[package["ImportPath"]] = {
58	            "dir": pathlib.Path(package["Dir"]).resolve(),
59	            "imports": set(
60	                dependency
61	                for key in ("Imports", "TestImports", "XTestImports")
62	                for dependency in package.get(key) or []
63	            ),
64	        }
65	    return packages
66	
67	
68	def decide(files, packages):
69	    if not files:
70	        return {"mode": "none"}
71	    by_dir = {info["dir"]: path for path, info in packages.items()}
72	    changed = set()
73	    for name in files:
74	        if not name.endswith(".go"):
75	            return {"mode": "full", "reason": f"non-Go change: {name}"}
76	        directory = (ROOT / name).parent.resolve()
77	        package = by_dir.get(directory)
78	        if package is None:
79	            # A .go file outside every listed package (deleted directory, new
80	            # package the listing has but the mapping missed, ignored tree).
81	            return {"mode": "full", "reason": f"unmapped Go file: {name}"}
82	        changed.add(package)
83	    # Reverse-import closure: every package whose compile or test inputs
84	    # include a changed package must re-run.
85	    affected = set(changed)
86	    grew = True
87	    while grew:
88	        grew = False
89	        for path, info in packages.items():
90	            if path in affected:
91	                continue
92	            if info["imports"] & affected:
93	                affected.add(path)
94	                grew = True
95	    return {"mode": "selected", "packages": sorted(affected)}
96	
97	
98	def main():
99	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
100	    parser.add_argument("--base", help="base commit for git diff")
101	    parser.add_argument("--head", default="HEAD", help="head commit for git diff")
102	    parser.add_argument(
103	        "--changed-files",
104	        help="newline-separated file list to use instead of git diff (tests)",
105	    )
106	    parser.add_argument("--go-command", default="go")
107	    args = parser.parse_args()
108	    if args.changed_files:
109	        files = [
110	            line
111	            for line in pathlib.Path(args.changed_files).read_text().splitlines()
112	            if line.strip()
113	        ]
114	    elif args.base:
115	        files = changed_files(args.base, args.head)
116	    else:
117	        parser.error("one of --base or --changed-files is required")
118	    decision = decide(files, load_packages(args.go_command))
119	    json.dump(decision, sys.stdout)
120	    print()
121	
122	
123	if __name__ == "__main__":
124	    main()
125

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Compile, hash, inventory, and plan the production Windows test shards."""
3	
4	from __future__ import annotations
5	
6	import argparse
7	import hashlib
8	import json
9	import os
10	import re
11	import shutil
12	import subprocess
13	import sys
14	import tempfile
15	import time
16	from pathlib import Path
17	from typing import Any, Iterable
18	
19	import plan_shards
20	
21	
22	PACKAGE_SCHEMA = "entire-brain.windows-ci.package-inventory.v1"
23	PREPARE_SCHEMA = "entire-brain.windows-ci.prepare-metadata.v1"
24	ROOT_PREFIXES = ("Test", "Example", "Fuzz")
25	TARGET_ENVIRONMENT = {"CGO_ENABLED": "1", "GOARCH": "amd64", "GOOS": "windows"}
26	TESTMAIN_SCHEMA = "entire-brain.windows-ci.testmain-inventory.v1"
27	
28	
29	def write_text(path: Path, value: str) -> None:
30	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
31	    path.write_text(value, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
32	
33	
34	def write_json(path: Path, value: Any) -> None:
35	    plan_shards.write_json(path, value)
36	
37	
38	def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
39	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
40	    with path.open("rb") as handle:
41	        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
42	            digest.update(chunk)
43	    return digest.hexdigest()
44	
45	
46	def decode_json_stream(value: str, label: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
47	    decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
48	    position = 0
49	    result: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
50	    while True:
51	        match = re.search(r"\S", value[position:])
52	        if match is None:
53	            break
54	        position += match.start()
55	        try:
56	            item, position = decoder.raw_decode(value, position)
57	        except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
58	            raise ValueError(f"{label}: invalid concatenated JSON at offset {position}: {error}") from error
59	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
60	            raise ValueError(f"{label}: JSON stream item is not an object")
61	        result.append(item)
62	    if not result:
63	        raise ValueError(f"{label}: JSON stream is empty")
64	    return result
65	
66	
67	def run_command(
68	    arguments: list[str],
69	    *,
70	    cwd: Path,
71	    environment: dict[str, str],
72	    stdout_path: Path | None = None,
73	    stderr_path: Path | None = None,
74	    stdin_text: str | None = None,
75	) -> tuple[subprocess.CompletedProcess[str], float]:
76	    started = time.monotonic()
77	    completed = subprocess.run(
78	        arguments,
79	        cwd=cwd,
80	        env=environment,
81	        text=True,
82	        encoding="utf-8",
83	        errors="strict",
84	        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
85	        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
86	        input=stdin_text,
87	        check=False,
88	    )
89	    duration = time.monotonic() - started
90	    if stdout_path is not None:
91	        write_text(stdout_path, completed.stdout)
92	    if stderr_path is not None:
93	        write_text(stderr_path, completed.stderr)
94	    return completed, duration
95	
96	
97	def require_success(completed: subprocess.CompletedProcess[str], label: str) -> None:
98	    if completed.returncode != 0:
99	        detail = completed.stderr.strip() or completed.stdout.strip()
100	        raise RuntimeError(f"{label} exited {completed.returncode}: {detail[:2000]}")
101	
102	
103	def require_tracked_worktree_clean(
104	    completed: subprocess.CompletedProcess[str], label: str
105	) -> None:
106	    require_success(completed, label)
107	    if completed.stdout.strip():
108	        raise RuntimeError(f"{label}: tracked worktree modifications detected")
109	
110	
111	def direct_test_environment(
112	    environment: dict[str, str], package_directory: Path, go_tool_directory: Path
113	) -> dict[str, str]:
114	    if not package_directory.is_absolute() or not go_tool_directory.is_absolute():
115	        raise ValueError("direct test environment requires absolute package and Go tool directories")
116	    result = dict(environment)
117	    result["PWD"] = str(package_directory)
118	    existing_path = result.get("PATH", "")
119	    result["PATH"] = str(go_tool_directory) + (os.pathsep + existing_path if existing_path else "")
120	    return result
121	
122	
123	def require_race_build(build_info: str) -> None:
124	    if not any(line.split() == ["build", "-race=true"] for line in build_info.splitlines()):
125	        raise RuntimeError("compiled test binary does not prove -race=true")
126	
127	
128	def require_coverage_build(build_info: str) -> None:
129	    if not any(line.split() == ["build", "-cover=true"] for line in build_info.splitlines()):
130	        raise RuntimeError("compiled test binary does not prove -cover=true")
131	
132	
133	def direct_listing_arguments(binary: Path) -> list[str]:
134	    return [str(binary), "-test.paniconexit0", "-test.list=."]
135	
136	
137	def repository_relative_directory(repository: Path, directory: str, label: str) -> str:
138	    resolved = Path(directory).resolve(strict=True)
139	    try:
140	        relative = resolved.relative_to(repository)
141	    except ValueError as error:
142	        raise ValueError(f"{label} directory is outside the repository: {resolved}") from error
143	    if not relative.parts:
144	        return "."
145	    if ".." in relative.parts:
146	        raise ValueError(f"{label} directory is unsafe: {relative}")
147	    return relative.as_posix()
148	
149	
150	def classify_listing(lines: Iterable[str], label: str) -> tuple[list[dict[str, str]], list[str]]:
151	    roots: list[dict[str, str]] = []
152	    benchmarks: list[str] = []
153	    unexpected: list[str] = []
154	    seen: set[str] = set()
155	    for raw in lines:
156	        name = raw.strip()
157	        if not name:
158	            continue
159	        if name in seen:
160	            raise ValueError(f"{label}: duplicate -test.list output {name!r}")
161	        seen.add(name)
162	        if name == "TestMain":
163	            unexpected.append(name)
164	        elif name.startswith("Benchmark"):
165	            benchmarks.append(name)
166	        else:
167	            kind = next((prefix for prefix in ROOT_PREFIXES if name.startswith(prefix)), None)
168	            if kind is None or any(character.isspace() for character in name):
169	                unexpected.append(name)
170	            else:
171	                roots.append({"name": name, "kind": kind})
172	    if unexpected:
173	        raise ValueError(f"{label}: unexpected -test.list output: {unexpected[:20]!r}")
174	    if not roots:
175	        raise ValueError(f"{label}: compiled binary listed no default-runnable roots")
176	    return sorted(roots, key=lambda item: item["name"]), sorted(benchmarks)
177	
178	
179	def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
180	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
181	    parser.add_argument("--repository", type=Path, required=True)
182	    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
183	    parser.add_argument("--settings", type=Path, required=True)
184	    parser.add_argument("--weights", type=Path, required=True)
185	    parser.add_argument("--expected-repository-sha", required=True)
186	    parser.add_argument("--go-command", default="go")
187	    return parser.parse_args(argv)
188	
189	
190	def prepare(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
191	    if sys.platform != "win32":
192	        raise RuntimeError("prepare.py must run on native Windows")
193	    repository = args.repository.resolve(strict=True)
194	    output = args.output.resolve()
195	    binaries = output / "binaries"
196	    inventories_dir = output / "inventories"
197	    logs = output / "logs"
198	    for directory in (binaries, inventories_dir, logs):
199	        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
200	
201	    settings_path = args.settings.resolve(strict=True)
202	    weights_path = args.weights.resolve(strict=True)
203	    settings = plan_shards.load_settings(settings_path)
204	    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", args.expected_repository_sha):
205	        raise ValueError("expected repository SHA must be 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters")
206	
207	    environment = dict(os.environ)
208	    environment.update({"GOOS": "windows", "GOARCH": "amd64", "CGO_ENABLED": "1"})
209	    go = shutil.which(args.go_command, path=environment.get("PATH"))
210	    if go is None:
211	        raise RuntimeError(f"cannot resolve Go command {args.go_command!r}")
212	    go = str(Path(go).resolve(strict=True))
213	    operations: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
214	
215	    clean_before, clean_before_seconds = run_command(
216	        ["git", "-C", str(repository), "status", "--porcelain=v1", "--untracked-files=no"],
217	        cwd=repository,
218	        environment=environment,
219	    )
220	    operations.append(
221	        {

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Select the Go packages a change set can affect, for PR test selection.
3	
4	Reads the changed file list (from git or --changed-files), maps every changed
5	.go file to its package, expands through the reverse import graph (production,
6	test, and external-test imports), and prints a JSON decision:
7	
8	  {"mode": "full"}                     — fall back to the complete suite
9	  {"mode": "none"}                     — no Go package is affected
10	  {"mode": "selected", "packages": []} — run exactly these packages
11	
12	The selection FAILS SAFE: any changed file that is not a .go file inside a
13	listed package directory — workflow edits, go.mod/go.sum, tools, embedded
14	assets, testdata — selects the full suite, because those inputs can change Go
15	behavior without changing a .go file. Selection must only ever narrow a run it
16	can prove is equivalent for the affected packages.
17	"""
18	import argparse
19	import json
20	import pathlib
21	import subprocess
22	import sys
23	
24	ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
25	
26	
27	def changed_files(base, head, cwd=ROOT):
28	    # --no-renames keeps a rename visible as an add plus a delete, so a .go
29	    # file moved between packages marks BOTH packages as changed. With rename
30	    # detection, --name-only lists only the destination and the source package
31	    # would silently keep its stale selection.
32	    output = subprocess.check_output(
33	        ["git", "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", f"{base}", f"{head}"],
34	        cwd=cwd,
35	        text=True,
36	    )
37	    return [line for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]
38	
39	
40	def load_packages(go):
41	    """Return {import_path: {dir, deps_on}} with reverse edges unexpanded."""
42	    output = subprocess.check_output(
43	        [go, "list", "-json=ImportPath,Dir,Imports,TestImports,XTestImports", "./..."],
44	        cwd=ROOT,
45	        text=True,
46	    )
47	    packages = {}
48	    decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
49	    index = 0
50	    while index < len(output):
51	        while index < len(output) and output[index] in " \r\n\t":
52	            index += 1
53	        if index >= len(output):
54	            break
55	        package, end = decoder.raw_decode(output, index)
56	        index = end
57	        packages[package["ImportPath"]] = {
58	            "dir": pathlib.Path(package["Dir"]).resolve(),
59	            "imports": set(
60	                dependency
61	                for key in ("Imports", "TestImports", "XTestImports")
62	                for dependency in package.get(key) or []
63	            ),
64	        }
65	    return packages
66	
67	
68	def decide(files, packages):
69	    if not files:
70	        return {"mode": "none"}
71	    by_dir = {info["dir"]: path for path, info in packages.items()}
72	    changed = set()
73	    for name in files:
74	        if not name.endswith(".go"):
75	            return {"mode": "full", "reason": f"non-Go change: {name}"}
76	        directory = (ROOT / name).parent.resolve()
77	        package = by_dir.get(directory)
78	        if package is None:
79	            # A .go file outside every listed package (deleted directory, new
80	            # package the listing has but the mapping missed, ignored tree).
81	            return {"mode": "full", "reason": f"unmapped Go file: {name}"}
82	        changed.add(package)
83	    # Reverse-import closure: every package whose compile or test inputs
84	    # include a changed package must re-run.
85	    affected = set(changed)
86	    grew = True
87	    while grew:
88	        grew = False
89	        for path, info in packages.items():
90	            if path in affected:
91	                continue
92	            if info["imports"] & affected:
93	                affected.add(path)
94	                grew = True
95	    return {"mode": "selected", "packages": sorted(affected)}
96	
97	
98	def main():
99	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
100	    parser.add_argument("--base", help="base commit for git diff")
101	    parser.add_argument("--head", default="HEAD", help="head commit for git diff")
102	    parser.add_argument(
103	        "--changed-files",
104	        help="newline-separated file list to use instead of git diff (tests)",
105	    )
106	    parser.add_argument("--go-command", default="go")
107	    args = parser.parse_args()
108	    if args.changed_files:
109	        files = [
110	            line
111	            for line in pathlib.Path(args.changed_files).read_text().splitlines()
112	            if line.strip()
113	        ]
114	    elif args.base:
115	        files = changed_files(args.base, args.head)
116	    else:
117	        parser.error("one of --base or --changed-files is required")
118	    decision = decide(files, load_packages(args.go_command))
119	    json.dump(decision, sys.stdout)
120	    print()
121	
122	
123	if __name__ == "__main__":
124	    main()

355	class _Trie:
356	    __slots__ = ("children", "terminal")
357	
358	    def __init__(self) -> None:
359	        self.children: dict[str, _Trie] = {}
360	        self.terminal = False
361	
362	
363	def _render_trie(node: _Trie) -> str:
364	    alternatives = [
365	        re.escape(character) + _render_trie(child)
366	        for character, child in sorted(node.children.items())
367	    ]
368	    if not alternatives:
369	        return ""
370	    body = alternatives[0] if len(alternatives) == 1 else "(" + "|".join(alternatives) + ")"
371	    return "(" + body + ")?" if node.terminal else body

374	def compressed_run_regex(names: Iterable[str]) -> str:
375	    ordered = sorted(set(names))
376	    if not ordered:
377	        raise ValueError("cannot create a run regex for no roots")
378	    root = _Trie()
379	    for name in ordered:
380	        node = root
381	        for character in name:
382	            node = node.children.setdefault(character, _Trie())
383	        node.terminal = True
384	    return "^" + _render_trie(root) + "$"

387	def _inventory_digest(inventories: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
388	    encoded = json.dumps(
389	        inventories, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")
390	    ).encode("utf-8")
391	    return hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()

394	def create_plan(
395	    inventories: list[dict[str, Any]],
396	    settings: dict[str, Any],
397	    weights: dict[tuple[str, str], float],
398	    weight_metadata: dict[str, Any],
399	) -> dict[str, Any]:
400	    if not inventories:
401	        raise ValueError("at least one compiled inventory is required")
402	    expected_config = {
403	        (item["importPath"], item["binaryName"])
404	        for item in settings["heavyPackages"]
405	    }
406	    actual_config = {(item["importPath"], item["binaryName"]) for item in inventories}
407	    if actual_config != expected_config:
408	        raise ValueError("compiled inventories do not exactly match configured heavy packages")
409	    expected_test_mains = {
410	        item["importPath"]: item["expectedTestMainDeclarations"]
411	        for item in settings["heavyPackages"]
412	    }
413	    for inventory in inventories:
414	        if inventory["testMainDeclarations"] != expected_test_mains[inventory["importPath"]]:
415	            raise ValueError(
416	                f"compiled TestMain declarations drifted for {inventory['importPath']}"
417	            )
418	    repository_shas = {item["repositorySha"] for item in inventories}
419	    go_versions = {item["goVersion"] for item in inventories}
420	    if len(repository_shas) != 1 or len(go_versions) != 1:
421	        raise ValueError("compiled inventories disagree on repository or Go version")
422	
423	    work: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
424	    used_weight_keys: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
425	    for inventory in inventories:
426	        for root in inventory["roots"]:
427	            key = (inventory["importPath"], root["name"])
428	            if key in weights:
429	                weight = weights[key]
430	                source = "historical-windows"
431	                used_weight_keys.add(key)
432	            else:
433	                weight = settings["defaultWeightSeconds"]
434	                source = "default-current-inventory"
435	            work.append(
436	                {
437	                    "importPath": inventory["importPath"],
438	                    "packageDirectoryRelative": inventory["packageDirectoryRelative"],
439	                    "binaryName": inventory["binaryName"],
440	                    "binarySha256": inventory["binarySha256"],
441	                    "name": root["name"],
442	                    "kind": root["kind"],
443	                    "weightSeconds": round(float(weight), 6),
444	                    "weightSource": source,
445	                }
446	            )
447	
448	    shard_count = settings["shardCount"]
449	    if len(work) < shard_count:
450	        raise ValueError(f"{len(work)} runnable roots cannot populate {shard_count} non-empty shards")
451	    work.sort(key=lambda item: (-item["weightSeconds"], item["importPath"], item["name"]))
452	    bins: list[list[dict[str, Any]]] = [[] for _ in range(shard_count)]
453	    totals = [0.0] * shard_count
454	    for item in work:
455	        destination = min(
456	            range(shard_count), key=lambda index: (totals[index], len(bins[index]), index)
457	        )
458	        bins[destination].append(item)
459	        totals[destination] += item["weightSeconds"]
460	
461	    shards: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
462	    for index, roots in enumerate(bins):
463	        by_package: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(list)
464	        for root in roots:
465	            by_package[root["importPath"]].append(root)
466	        assignments: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
467	        for package in sorted(by_package):
468	            package_roots = sorted(by_package[package], key=lambda item: item["name"])
469	            assignments.append(
470	                {
471	                    "importPath": package,
472	                    "packageDirectoryRelative": package_roots[0]["packageDirectoryRelative"],
473	                    "binaryName": package_roots[0]["binaryName"],
474	                    "binarySha256": package_roots[0]["binarySha256"],
475	                    "runRegex": compressed_run_regex(item["name"] for item in package_roots),
476	                    "roots": [
477	                        {
478	                            "name": item["name"],
479	                            "kind": item["kind"],
480	                            "weightSeconds": item["weightSeconds"],
481	                            "weightSource": item["weightSource"],
482	                        }
483	                        for item in package_roots
484	                    ],
485	                }
486	            )
487	        shards.append(
488	            {
489	                "index": index,
490	                "estimatedWeightSeconds": round(totals[index], 6),
491	                "rootCount": len(roots),
492	                "assignments": assignments,
493	            }
494	        )
495	
496	    unused = sorted(f"{package}::{name}" for package, name in set(weights) - used_weight_keys)
497	    packages = [
498	        {
499	            "importPath": item["importPath"],
500	            "packageDirectoryRelative": item["packageDirectoryRelative"],
501	            "binaryName": item["binaryName"],
502	            "binarySha256": item["binarySha256"],
503	            "binarySizeBytes": item["binarySizeBytes"],
504	            "rootCount": len(item["roots"]),
505	            "excludedBenchmarkCount": len(item["excludedBenchmarks"]),
506	            "testMainDeclarations": item["testMainDeclarations"],
507	        }
508	        for item in inventories
509	    ]
510	    return {
511	        "schema": PLAN_SCHEMA,
512	        "algorithm": "deterministic-longest-processing-time-first-v1",
513	        "repositorySha": next(iter(repository_shas)),
514	        "goVersion": next(iter(go_versions)),
515	        "targetEnvironment": dict(TARGET_ENVIRONMENT),
516	        "inventorySetSha256": _inventory_digest(inventories),
517	        "shardCount": shard_count,
518	        "rootCount": len(work),
519	        "packageCount": len(inventories),
520	        "settings": {
521	            "timeout": settings["timeout"],
522	            "commandLineLimit": settings["commandLineLimit"],
523	            "shuffle": settings["shuffle"],
524	            "testParallel": settings["testParallel"],
525	            "goMaxProcs": settings["goMaxProcs"],
526	            "defaultWeightSeconds": settings["defaultWeightSeconds"],
527	            "coverageMode": COVERAGE_MODE,
528	            "coveragePackages": COVERAGE_PACKAGES,
529	        },
530	        "historicalWeights": {
531	            **weight_metadata,
532	            "usedCount": len(used_weight_keys),
533	            "defaultedCount": len(work) - len(used_weight_keys),
534	            "unusedKeys": unused,
535	        },
536	        "packages": packages,
537	        "shards": shards,
538	    }

541	def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
542	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
543	    parser.add_argument("--settings", type=Path, required=True)
544	    parser.add_argument("--weights", type=Path, required=True)
545	    parser.add_argument("--inventory", action="append", type=Path, required=True)
546	    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
547	    return parser.parse_args(argv)

550	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
551	    args = parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
552	    try:
553	        settings = load_settings(args.settings)
554	        weights, metadata = load_weights(args.weights)
555	        inventories = load_inventories(args.inventory)
556	        plan = create_plan(inventories, settings, weights, metadata)
557	        write_json(args.output, plan)
558	    except (ValueError, OSError) as error:
559	        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
560	        return 2
561	    return 0

13	from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

17	SETTINGS_SCHEMA = "entire-brain.windows-ci.settings.v1"
18	WEIGHTS_SCHEMA = "entire-brain.windows-ci.historical-weights.v1"
19	INVENTORY_SCHEMA = "entire-brain.windows-ci.compiled-inventory.v1"

24	_TIMEOUT = re.compile(r"^[1-9][0-9]*(?:ns|us|µs|ms|s|m|h)$")
25	_SHA = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")
26	_SHA256 = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
27	TARGET_ENVIRONMENT = {"GOOS": "windows", "GOARCH": "amd64", "CGO_ENABLED": "1"}

29	
30	def read_json(path: Path) -> Any:
31	    try:
32	        with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig") as handle:
33	            return json.load(handle)
34	    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
35	        raise ValueError(f"cannot read JSON {path}: {error}") from error
36	
37	
38	def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
39	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
40	    try:
41	        with path.open("rb") as handle:
42	            for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
43	                digest.update(chunk)
44	    except OSError as error:
45	        raise ValueError(f"cannot hash {path}: {error}") from error
46	    return digest.hexdigest()

48	
49	def write_json(path: Path, value: Any) -> None:
50	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
51	    temporary = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")
52	    with temporary.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
53	        json.dump(value, handle, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
54	        handle.write("\n")
55	    temporary.replace(path)

58	def _safe_relative_directory(value: Any, label: str) -> str:
59	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value or "\\" in value:
60	        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be a non-empty normalized POSIX path")
61	    path = PurePosixPath(value)
62	    if path.is_absolute() or ".." in path.parts or "." in path.parts:
63	        raise ValueError(f"{label} is unsafe: {value!r}")
64	    return value

67	def load_settings(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
68	    value = read_json(path)
69	    if not isinstance(value, dict) or value.get("schema") != SETTINGS_SCHEMA:
70	        raise ValueError(f"{path}: unexpected settings schema")
71	    shard_count = value.get("shardCount")
72	    default_weight = value.get("defaultWeightSeconds")
73	    command_limit = value.get("commandLineLimit")
74	    timeout = value.get("timeout")
75	    if not isinstance(shard_count, int) or isinstance(shard_count, bool) or not 1 <= shard_count <= 64:
76	        raise ValueError(f"{path}: shardCount must be an integer from 1 through 64")
77	    if (

355	class _Trie:
356	    __slots__ = ("children", "terminal")
357	
358	    def __init__(self) -> None:
359	        self.children: dict[str, _Trie] = {}
360	        self.terminal = False
361	
362	
363	def _render_trie(node: _Trie) -> str:
364	    alternatives = [
365	        re.escape(character) + _render_trie(child)
366	        for character, child in sorted(node.children.items())
367	    ]
368	    if not alternatives:
369	        return ""
370	    body = alternatives[0] if len(alternatives) == 1 else "(" + "|".join(alternatives) + ")"
371	    return "(" + body + ")?" if node.terminal else body

374	def compressed_run_regex(names: Iterable[str]) -> str:
375	    ordered = sorted(set(names))
376	    if not ordered:
377	        raise ValueError("cannot create a run regex for no roots")
378	    root = _Trie()
379	    for name in ordered:
380	        node = root
381	        for character in name:
382	            node = node.children.setdefault(character, _Trie())
383	        node.terminal = True
384	    return "^" + _render_trie(root) + "$"

387	def _inventory_digest(inventories: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
388	    encoded = json.dumps(
389	        inventories, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")
390	    ).encode("utf-8")
391	    return hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()

394	def create_plan(
395	    inventories: list[dict[str, Any]],
396	    settings: dict[str, Any],
397	    weights: dict[tuple[str, str], float],
398	    weight_metadata: dict[str, Any],
399	) -> dict[str, Any]:
400	    if not inventories:
401	        raise ValueError("at least one compiled inventory is required")
402	    expected_config = {
403	        (item["importPath"], item["binaryName"])
404	        for item in settings["heavyPackages"]
405	    }
406	    actual_config = {(item["importPath"], item["binaryName"]) for item in inventories}
407	    if actual_config != expected_config:
408	        raise ValueError("compiled inventories do not exactly match configured heavy packages")
409	    expected_test_mains = {
410	        item["importPath"]: item["expectedTestMainDeclarations"]
411	        for item in settings["heavyPackages"]
412	    }
413	    for inventory in inventories:
414	        if inventory["testMainDeclarations"] != expected_test_mains[inventory["importPath"]]:
415	            raise ValueError(
416	                f"compiled TestMain declarations drifted for {inventory['importPath']}"
417	            )
418	    repository_shas = {item["repositorySha"] for item in inventories}
419	    go_versions = {item["goVersion"] for item in inventories}
420	    if len(repository_shas) != 1 or len(go_versions) != 1:
421	        raise ValueError("compiled inventories disagree on repository or Go version")
422	
423	    work: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
424	    used_weight_keys: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
425	    for inventory in inventories:
426	        for root in inventory["roots"]:
427	            key = (inventory["importPath"], root["name"])
428	            if key in weights:
429	                weight = weights[key]
430	                source = "historical-windows"
431	                used_weight_keys.add(key)
432	            else:
433	                weight = settings["defaultWeightSeconds"]
434	                source = "default-current-inventory"
435	            work.append(
436	                {
437	                    "importPath": inventory["importPath"],
438	                    "packageDirectoryRelative": inventory["packageDirectoryRelative"],
439	                    "binaryName": inventory["binaryName"],
440	                    "binarySha256": inventory["binarySha256"],
441	                    "name": root["name"],
442	                    "kind": root["kind"],
443	                    "weightSeconds": round(float(weight), 6),
444	                    "weightSource": source,
445	                }
446	            )
447	
448	    shard_count = settings["shardCount"]
449	    if len(work) < shard_count:
450	        raise ValueError(f"{len(work)} runnable roots cannot populate {shard_count} non-empty shards")
451	    work.sort(key=lambda item: (-item["weightSeconds"], item["importPath"], item["name"]))
452	    bins: list[list[dict[str, Any]]] = [[] for _ in range(shard_count)]
453	    totals = [0.0] * shard_count
454	    for item in work:
455	        destination = min(
456	            range(shard_count), key=lambda index: (totals[index], len(bins[index]), index)
457	        )
458	        bins[destination].append(item)
459	        totals[destination] += item["weightSeconds"]
460	
461	    shards: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
462	    for index, roots in enumerate(bins):
463	        by_package: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(list)
464	        for root in roots:
465	            by_package[root["importPath"]].append(root)
466	        assignments: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
467	        for package in sorted(by_package):
468	            package_roots = sorted(by_package[package], key=lambda item: item["name"])
469	            assignments.append(
470	                {
471	                    "importPath": package,
472	                    "packageDirectoryRelative": package_roots[0]["packageDirectoryRelative"],
473	                    "binaryName": package_roots[0]["binaryName"],
474	                    "binarySha256": package_roots[0]["binarySha256"],
475	                    "runRegex": compressed_run_regex(item["name"] for item in package_roots),
476	                    "roots": [
477	                        {
478	                            "name": item["name"],
479	                            "kind": item["kind"],
480	                            "weightSeconds": item["weightSeconds"],
481	                            "weightSource": item["weightSource"],
482	                        }
483	                        for item in package_roots
484	                    ],
485	                }
486	            )
487	        shards.append(
488	            {
489	                "index": index,
490	                "estimatedWeightSeconds": round(totals[index], 6),
491	                "rootCount": len(roots),
492	                "assignments": assignments,
493	            }
494	        )
495	
496	    unused = sorted(f"{package}::{name}" for package, name in set(weights) - used_weight_keys)
497	    packages = [
498	        {
499	            "importPath": item["importPath"],
500	            "packageDirectoryRelative": item["packageDirectoryRelative"],
501	            "binaryName": item["binaryName"],
502	            "binarySha256": item["binarySha256"],
503	            "binarySizeBytes": item["binarySizeBytes"],
504	            "rootCount": len(item["roots"]),
505	            "excludedBenchmarkCount": len(item["excludedBenchmarks"]),
506	            "testMainDeclarations": item["testMainDeclarations"],
507	        }
508	        for item in inventories
509	    ]
510	    return {
511	        "schema": PLAN_SCHEMA,
512	        "algorithm": "deterministic-longest-processing-time-first-v1",
513	        "repositorySha": next(iter(repository_shas)),
514	        "goVersion": next(iter(go_versions)),
515	        "targetEnvironment": dict(TARGET_ENVIRONMENT),
516	        "inventorySetSha256": _inventory_digest(inventories),
517	        "shardCount": shard_count,
518	        "rootCount": len(work),
519	        "packageCount": len(inventories),
520	        "settings": {
521	            "timeout": settings["timeout"],
522	            "commandLineLimit": settings["commandLineLimit"],
523	            "shuffle": settings["shuffle"],
524	            "testParallel": settings["testParallel"],
525	            "goMaxProcs": settings["goMaxProcs"],
526	            "defaultWeightSeconds": settings["defaultWeightSeconds"],
527	            "coverageMode": COVERAGE_MODE,
528	            "coveragePackages": COVERAGE_PACKAGES,
529	        },
530	        "historicalWeights": {
531	            **weight_metadata,
532	            "usedCount": len(used_weight_keys),
533	            "defaultedCount": len(work) - len(used_weight_keys),
534	            "unusedKeys": unused,
535	        },
536	        "packages": packages,
537	        "shards": shards,
538	    }

541	def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
542	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
543	    parser.add_argument("--settings", type=Path, required=True)
544	    parser.add_argument("--weights", type=Path, required=True)
545	    parser.add_argument("--inventory", action="append", type=Path, required=True)
546	    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
547	    return parser.parse_args(argv)

550	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
551	    args = parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
552	    try:
553	        settings = load_settings(args.settings)
554	        weights, metadata = load_weights(args.weights)
555	        inventories = load_inventories(args.inventory)
556	        plan = create_plan(inventories, settings, weights, metadata)
557	        write_json(args.output, plan)
558	    except (ValueError, OSError) as error:
559	        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
560	        return 2
561	    return 0

Now I'm piecing together the architecture: prepare.py inventories packages and separates heavy ones, while run_other.py presumably runs go test on the non-heavy packages from that inventory. I'm also noting that create_plan enforces an invariant where work count can't fall below shard count, so I need to figure out how shardCount gets adjusted when the selection is small.

Constraint 2 complicates this — an empty selection still must emit a valid minimal plan where shards execute zero roots and exit cleanly, but create_plan currently requires at least one inventory, non-empty roots, and work >= shard_count, and the workflow's shard-matrix validation requires a positive shard count matching the index count. Given constraint 4 says selection can't change how any planned root is compiled, named, or hashed, I'm considering filtering only at the inventory or plan level — but since verify_results.py cross-checks plan, package-inventory, and shard results for exact coverage, any filtering needs to keep all these in sync, so I should look at run_other.py and run_shards next.

The real snag is that create_plan also checks that compiled heavy-package inventories exactly match the configured set, so skipping compilation of unaffected heavy packages to save time would break that invariant — filtering roots within a package doesn't help since compile time dominates the prepare job's runtime anyway.

So the design falls into place: prepare still compiles and inventories everything unchanged, but the plan itself only includes roots from affected heavy packages, and run_other gets filtered to affected non-heavy packages. I'm now thinking through prepare.py's handling of the affected.json input — missing, malformed, or non-"selected" modes fall back to full behavior, while "selected" mode extracts the set of affected import paths, and I need to double-check how a "none" mode should be treated given that affected.py could emit it when no files changed.

For applying the filtering, I realize I can't just empty out roots per heavy package in the inventories since load_inventories rejects empty roots, and dropping whole inventories would break create_plan's exact-match check against expected_config — so the filtering needs to happen at the plan level after inventories are loaded, not by mutating the inventories themselves.

So I'm thinking of adding an optional selected_packages parameter to create_plan that filters work to only roots whose importPath is in the selected set, while keeping shard_count valid — if the filtered work is smaller than shard_count I may need to shrink shard_count, since the workflow's shard-matrix validation just needs shard indexes matching shardCount and at least one shard, so an empty selection could still produce a minimal valid plan with one shard executing zero roots and exiting cleanly. I still need to check whether other consumers of the plan, like run_shard.py and verify_results, tolerate a zero-root shard.

Now I'm wondering whether verify_results checks full package coverage against package-inventory.json even when run_other has skipped unaffected packages, and whether I'll need to add selection metadata into plan.json so run_other.py and verify can both honor the selection — which means I need to actually read through run_other.py, run_shard.py, verify_results.py, and the workflow contract test to be sure.

221	def run(args: argparse.Namespace, metadata: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
222	    if sys.platform != "win32":
223	        raise RuntimeError("run_shard.py must run on native Windows")
224	    repository = args.repository.resolve(strict=True)
225	    bundle = args.bundle.resolve(strict=True)
226	    output = args.output.resolve()
227	    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
228	    plan_path = bundle / "plan.json"
229	    plan = read_json(plan_path)
230	    if not isinstance(plan, dict) or plan.get("schema") != PLAN_SCHEMA:
231	        raise ValueError("unexpected or missing shard plan schema")
232	    if plan.get("targetEnvironment") != TARGET_ENVIRONMENT:
233	        raise ValueError("shard plan target is not exactly windows/amd64 with CGO_ENABLED=1")
234	    if not isinstance(args.shard_index, int) or not 0 <= args.shard_index < plan.get("shardCount", -1):
235	        raise ValueError(f"shard index {args.shard_index} is outside the plan")
236	    shards = [item for item in plan.get("shards", []) if item.get("index") == args.shard_index]
237	    if len(shards) != 1:
238	        raise ValueError(f"plan does not contain exactly one shard {args.shard_index}")
239	    shard = shards[0]
240	    assignments = shard.get("assignments")
241	    if not isinstance(assignments, list) or not assignments:
242	        raise ValueError(f"shard {args.shard_index} has no assignments")
243	    settings = plan.get("settings")
244	    if not isinstance(settings, dict) or settings.get("shuffle") != "off":
245	        raise ValueError("plan does not preserve shuffle=off semantics")
246	    if (
247	        settings.get("coverageMode") != COVERAGE_MODE
248	        or settings.get("coveragePackages") != COVERAGE_PACKAGES
249	    ):
250	        raise ValueError("plan does not require atomic cross-package coverage")
251	    timeout = settings.get("timeout")
252	    command_limit = settings.get("commandLineLimit")
253	    if not isinstance(timeout, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[1-9][0-9]*(?:ns|us|µs|ms|s|m|h)", timeout):
254	        raise ValueError("plan has an invalid timeout")
255	    if not isinstance(command_limit, int) or not 1024 <= command_limit <= 32767:
256	        raise ValueError("plan has an invalid Windows command-line limit")
257	
258	    environment = dict(os.environ)
259	    environment.update({"GOOS": "windows", "GOARCH": "amd64", "CGO_ENABLED": "1"})
260	    go_max_procs = settings.get("goMaxProcs")
261	    if go_max_procs is not None:
262	        if not isinstance(go_max_procs, int) or isinstance(go_max_procs, bool) or go_max_procs <= 0:
263	            raise ValueError("plan has invalid goMaxProcs")
264	        environment["GOMAXPROCS"] = str(go_max_procs)
265	    go = shutil.which(args.go_command, path=environment.get("PATH"))
266	    if go is None:
267	        raise RuntimeError(f"cannot resolve Go command {args.go_command!r}")
268	    go = str(Path(go).resolve(strict=True))
269	    repository_sha = checked_repository_sha(repository, environment)
270	    if repository_sha != args.expected_repository_sha or repository_sha != plan.get("repositorySha"):
271	        raise RuntimeError(
272	            f"repository SHA mismatch: checkout={repository_sha!r}, expected={args.expected_repository_sha!r}, plan={plan.get('repositorySha')!r}"
273	        )
274	    go_version = checked_go_version(go, repository, environment)
275	    if go_version != plan.get("goVersion"):
276	        raise RuntimeError(f"Go toolchain mismatch: runner={go_version!r}, plan={plan.get('goVersion')!r}")
277	    target_environment, go_tool_directory = checked_go_environment(go, repository, environment)
278	    if target_environment != plan.get("targetEnvironment"):
279	        raise RuntimeError("runner target Go environment differs from the plan")
280	    require_tracked_worktree_clean(repository, environment, "tracked worktree precondition")
281	
282	    metadata.update(
283	        {
284	            "repositorySha": repository_sha,
285	            "goVersion": go_version,
286	            "targetEnvironment": target_environment,
287	            "goToolDirectory": str(go_tool_directory),
288	            "trackedWorktreeCleanBefore": True,
289	            "planSha256": sha256_file(plan_path),
290	            "shardIndex": args.shard_index,
291	            "shardCount": plan["shardCount"],
292	            "commandLineLimit": command_limit,
293	            "timeout": timeout,
294	            "shuffle": "off",
295	            "testParallel": settings.get("testParallel"),
296	            "goMaxProcs": go_max_procs,
297	            "coverageMode": COVERAGE_MODE,
298	            "coveragePackages": COVERAGE_PACKAGES,
299	        }
300	    )
301	    combined_events = output / "shard-events.jsonl"
302	    combined_events.write_bytes(b"")
303	    coverage_directory = (output / "coverage").resolve()
304	    try:
305	        coverage_directory.relative_to(output)
306	    except ValueError as error:
307	        raise ValueError("coverage directory escaped result artifact") from error
308	    coverage_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
309	    final_exit = 0
310	    try:
311	        clean = subprocess.run(
312	            [go, "clean", "-testcache"],
313	            cwd=repository,
314	            env=environment,
315	            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
316	            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
317	            check=False,
318	        )
319	        (output / "clean-testcache.stdout.log").write_bytes(clean.stdout)
320	        (output / "clean-testcache.stderr.log").write_bytes(clean.stderr)
321	        metadata["cleanTestCacheExitCode"] = clean.returncode
322	        if clean.returncode != 0:
323	            return clean.returncode
324	
325	        for position, assignment in enumerate(assignments):
326	            package = assignment.get("importPath")
327	            binary_name = assignment.get("binaryName")
328	            expected_binary_hash = assignment.get("binarySha256")
329	            run_regex = assignment.get("runRegex")
330	            roots = assignment.get("roots")
331	            if not isinstance(package, str) or not package:
332	                raise ValueError(f"assignment {position} has no import path")
333	            if (
334	                not isinstance(binary_name, str)
335	                or Path(binary_name).name != binary_name
336	                or "/" in binary_name
337	                or "\\" in binary_name
338	            ):
339	                raise ValueError(f"assignment {position} has unsafe binary name")
340	            if not isinstance(expected_binary_hash, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", expected_binary_hash):
341	                raise ValueError(f"assignment {position} has invalid binary hash")
342	            if not isinstance(run_regex, str) or not run_regex.startswith("^") or not run_regex.endswith("$"):
343	                raise ValueError(f"assignment {position} has invalid run regex")
344	            if not isinstance(roots, list) or not roots:
345	                raise ValueError(f"assignment {position} has no runnable roots")
346	            package_directory = safe_repository_directory(
347	                repository, assignment.get("packageDirectoryRelative")
348	            )
349	            binary = (bundle / "binaries" / binary_name).resolve(strict=True)
350	            try:
351	                binary.relative_to((bundle / "binaries").resolve(strict=True))
352	            except ValueError as error:
353	                raise ValueError(f"binary escaped bundle: {binary}") from error
354	            actual_binary_hash = sha256_file(binary)
355	            if actual_binary_hash != expected_binary_hash:
356	                raise RuntimeError(
357	                    f"binary hash mismatch for {package}: {actual_binary_hash} != {expected_binary_hash}"
358	                )
359	
360	            test_parallel = settings.get("testParallel")
361	            if test_parallel is not None and (
362	                not isinstance(test_parallel, int)
363	                or isinstance(test_parallel, bool)
364	                or test_parallel <= 0
365	            ):
366	                raise ValueError("plan has invalid testParallel")
367	            coverage_path = (
368	                coverage_directory
369	                / f"shard-{args.shard_index:03d}-process-{position:02d}.out"
370	            )
371	            coverage_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
372	            command_arguments = shard_command_arguments(
373	                package, binary, timeout, run_regex, test_parallel, coverage_path
374	            )
375	            command_units = command_line_utf16_units(go, command_arguments)
376	            if command_units > command_limit:
377	                raise RuntimeError(
378	                    f"serialized Windows command line for {package} is {command_units} UTF-16 units, above {command_limit}; refusing implicit batching"
379	                )
380	
381	            stem = f"{position:02d}-{re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]', '_', package)}"
382	            stdout_path = output / f"{stem}.jsonl"
383	            stderr_path = output / f"{stem}.stderr.log"
384	            direct_environment = direct_test_environment(
385	                environment, package_directory, go_tool_directory
386	            )
387	            started = time.monotonic()
388	            with stdout_path.open("wb") as stdout, stderr_path.open("wb") as stderr:
389	                completed = subprocess.run(
390	                    [go, *command_arguments],
391	                    cwd=package_directory,
392	                    env=direct_environment,
393	                    stdout=stdout,
394	                    stderr=stderr,
395	                    check=False,
396	                )
397	            duration = time.monotonic() - started
398	            coverage_error = None
399	            try:
400	                coverage_profile, coverage_sha256 = coverage_profile_metadata(
401	                    output, coverage_path
402	                )
403	            except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as error:
404	                if completed.returncode == 0:
405	                    raise
406	                # Crashes, race-runtime exits and timeouts can bypass Go's
407	                # profile flush. Preserve their actual failure and events, and
408	                # still execute the remaining packages assigned to this shard.
409	                # A null profile is diagnostic evidence, never valid coverage.
410	                coverage_profile, coverage_sha256 = None, None
411	                coverage_error = str(error)
412	            content = stdout_path.read_bytes()
413	            with combined_events.open("ab") as combined:
414	                combined.write(content)
415	                if content and not content.endswith(b"\n"):
416	                    combined.write(b"\n")
417	            invocation = {
418	                "package": package,
419	                "binaryName": binary_name,
420	                "binarySha256": actual_binary_hash,
421	                "rootCount": len(roots),
422	                "commandLineUtf16Units": command_units,
423	                "durationSeconds": round(duration, 6),
424	                "exitCode": completed.returncode,
425	                "paniconexit0": "-test.paniconexit0" in command_arguments,
426	                "workingDirectoryRelative": assignment.get("packageDirectoryRelative"),
427	                "pwdMatchesPackageDirectory": direct_environment.get("PWD")
428	                == str(package_directory),
429	                "goToolDirectoryPrependedToPath": direct_environment.get("PATH", "").split(
430	                    os.pathsep, 1
431	                )[0]
432	                == str(go_tool_directory),
433	                "coverageProfile": coverage_profile,
434	                "coverageSha256": coverage_sha256,
435	            }
436	            if coverage_error is not None:
437	                invocation["coverageError"] = coverage_error
438	            metadata["invocations"].append(invocation)
439	            write_json(output / "shard-metadata.json", metadata)
440	            if completed.returncode != 0 and final_exit == 0:
441	                final_exit = completed.returncode
442	        return final_exit
443	    finally:
444	        require_tracked_worktree_clean(repository, environment, "tracked worktree postcondition")
445	        metadata["trackedWorktreeCleanAfter"] = True
446	        repository_sha_after = checked_repository_sha(repository, environment)
447	        metadata["repositoryShaAfter"] = repository_sha_after
448	        if repository_sha_after != repository_sha:
449	            raise RuntimeError(
450	                f"repository SHA changed during shard execution: {repository_sha!r} -> {repository_sha_after!r}"
451	            )
452	
453	
454	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
455	    args = parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
456	    output = args.output.resolve()
457	    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
458	    metadata: dict[str, Any] = {
459	        "schema": RUN_SCHEMA,
460	        "exitCode": None,
461	        "errors": [],
462	        "invocations": [],
463	        "cleanTestCacheExitCode": None,
464	        "trackedWorktreeCleanBefore": None,
465	        "trackedWorktreeCleanAfter": None,
466	        "repositoryShaAfter": None,
467	    }
468	    try:
469	        exit_code = run(args, metadata)
470	    except Exception as error:
471	        metadata["errors"].append(str(error))
472	        exit_code = 2
473	        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
474	    metadata["exitCode"] = exit_code
475	    write_json(output / "shard-metadata.json", metadata)
476	    return exit_code
477	
478	
479	if __name__ == "__main__":
480	    raise SystemExit(main())

32	def write_json(path: Path, value: Any) -> None:
33	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

41	def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
42	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
43	    with path.open("rb") as handle:
44	        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
45	            digest.update(chunk)
46	    return digest.hexdigest()

I'm also noting that create_plan enforces an invariant where work count can't fall below shard count, so I need to figure out how shardCount gets adjusted when the selection is small.

Constraint 2 complicates this — an empty selection still must emit a valid minimal plan where shards execute zero roots and exit cleanly, but create_plan currently requires at least one inventory, non-empty roots, and work >= shard_count, and the workflow's shard-matrix validation requires a positive shard count matching the index count. Given constraint 4 says selection can't change how any planned root is compiled, named, or hashed, I'm considering filtering only at the inventory or plan level — but since verify_results.py cross-checks plan, package-inventory, and shard results for exact coverage, any filtering needs to keep all these in sync, so I should look at run_other.py and run_shards next.

The real snag is that create_plan also checks that compiled heavy-package inventories exactly match the configured set, so skipping compilation of unaffected heavy packages to save time would break that invariant — filtering roots within a package doesn't help since compile time dominates the prepare job's runtime anyway.

So the design falls into place: prepare still compiles and inventories everything unchanged, but the plan itself only includes roots from affected heavy packages, and run_other gets filtered to affected non-heavy packages. I'm now thinking through prepare.py's handling of the affected.json input — missing, malformed, or non-"selected" modes fall back to full behavior, while "selected" mode extracts the set of affected import paths, and I need to double-check how a "none" mode should be treated given that affected.py could emit it when no files changed.

For applying the filtering, I realize I can't just empty out roots per heavy package in the inventories since load_inventories rejects empty roots, and dropping whole inventories would break create_plan's exact-match check against expected_config — so the filtering needs to happen at the plan level after inventories are loaded, not by mutating the inventories themselves.

So I'm thinking of adding an optional selected_packages parameter to create_plan that filters work to only roots whose importPath is in the selected set, while keeping shard_count valid — if the filtered work is smaller than shard_count I may need to shrink shard_count, since the workflow's shard-matrix validation just needs shard indexes matching shardCount and at least one shard, so an empty selection could still produce a minimal valid plan with one shard executing zero roots and exiting cleanly. I still need to check whether other consumers of the plan, like run_shard.py and verify_results, tolerate a zero-root shard.

Now I'm wondering whether verify_results checks full package coverage against package-inventory.json even when run_other has skipped unaffected packages, and whether I'll need to add selection metadata into plan.json so run_other.py and verify can both honor the selection — which means I need to actually read through run_other.py, run_shard.py, verify_results.py, and the workflow contract test to be sure.

41	def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
42	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
43	    with path.open("rb") as handle:
44	        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
45	            digest.update(chunk)
46	    return digest.hexdigest()

49	def coverage_profile_metadata(output: Path, profile: Path) -> tuple[str, str]:
50	    output = output.resolve(strict=True)

This is much bigger than the task framing suggested — verify_results.py deeply assumes a full plan, checking that the plan's root count matches all compiled inventory roots, that no compiled roots are omitted, that shard counts align with settings, and that every shard has non-empty assignments, plus that expected packages match everything non-header related.

The task's non-goals never actually mention verify_results.py, yet it runs on every PR and would hard-fail against a filtered plan. The stated goal is really about the Windows plan containing only affected roots so shards finish quickly, but verify_results is a consumer of that plan, so I need to figure out whether making run_shard/run_other tolerant is actually sufficient or whether verify_results also needs updating.

I'm thinking the cleanest path is to make selection a first-class concept in the plan itself, and have prepare.py copy affected.json into the bundle so verify can cross-check the selection against known affected packages. Then verify_results' validate_plan would need to recognize a selection field, validate its shape, and filter expected roots down to only the selected packages.

I also need to account for shardCount being recomputed under selection as the min of settings and the selected root count, and for shards being allowed to have zero assignments when selection trims things down. That raises an edge case: verify_shards currently calls read_jsonl unconditionally, which will error on an empty shard-events.jsonl since run_shard writes an empty byte stream for shards with no assignments — I'll need to guard against that.

For verify_other, when the non-heavy package selection is empty, run_other skips the go test step and leaves testExitCode as None, which breaks the required-zero-exit check. I think verify_other needs a dedicated branch for the empty-selection case, expecting exitCode 0 and an empty expectedPackages list, though I'm not yet sure whether other-events.jsonl still gets written in that scenario.

For merge_coverage_profiles, the expected count is heavy_process_count plus two, where the extra two cover the non-heavy profile and a binary contract file.

With an empty non-heavy selection, there's no other.out profile to merge, so the expected count needs to shrink to heavy plus one (keeping the binary contract, since that step always runs). I also need to zero out nonheavy_profile_count in the environment, and check that test_workflow_contract.py doesn't pin the workflow structure in a way that breaks this.

Now I'm sketching out the selection-parsing logic in prepare.py -- a function that reads the affected-packages text and returns either a set of package names or None to signal a full run.

I'm defining the fail-safe rules: malformed JSON, wrong mode, or an invalid/missing packages list all fall back to a full run, since an empty package list under "selected" mode is inherently inconsistent with how affected.py works. Then in prepare(), I'm wiring this in so that a successful selection builds the plan with just those packages and bundles the affected.json file alongside the usual metadata.

I also need prepare to accept an `--affected` path argument, read and parse that file, and treat any read error as a reason to fall back to full mode with a warning. Another edge case I should guard against: if a selected package isn't actually present in the repo's go list output, that mismatch is itself an inconsistency, so it should trigger the same fail-safe fallback to a full run.

For create_plan, I'm adding a selected_packages parameter that, when provided, filters the work list down to only the matching import paths before shard count logic proceeds unchanged.

When selection mode is active, the plan dict should include a selection block with the full affected package set (not just heavy ones), since run_other needs the complete set to filter non-heavy packages, making the plan the single source of truth for both executors and the verifier.

I'm confirming rootCount tracking and unused-weights handling stay consistent with the filtered work set automatically, and that selection=None preserves byte-identical behavior. Now I'm turning to run_shard.py, allowing empty assignments when a selection dict is present in the plan...

For run_other.py, I'm validating that any selection present in the plan must have the correct shape — a dict with mode "selected" and a list of string packages — otherwise raising an error, since a malformed selection should fail the job closed rather than silently falling back to running everything, matching the harness's fail-safe philosophy.

If the filtered package list ends up empty, I'm thinking through how to keep the metadata consistent: setting expectedPackages to the empty list, packageCount to 0, and still writing an empty other-events.jsonl so verification finds an events file. The tricky part is testExitCode — setting it to 0 for a skipped run feels like a small lie, but it signals "nothing needed to run, success," so I'm weighing whether verify_other should branch differently to handle this case honestly.

I'll keep running go clean as usual for consistency, but skip the actual go test invocation entirely, writing an empty events file and setting testExitCode to 0 with empty testArguments. For verify_other's empty-case branch, I need it to expect an empty package list, skip coverage profile checks since there's nothing to cover, and skip the testArguments comparison accordingly.

I also need to handle read_jsonl gracefully when the file is empty rather than raising, and make sure the coverageProfile check still fires correctly if it's expected to be "coverage/other.out". For merge_coverage_profiles, I'm working out the expected count formula, parameterizing it based on heavy_process_count plus a fixed offset.

If the selection reduces both heavy and non-heavy processes to zero, the profile list falls back to just the instrumented binary contracts, which coverage_report.read_profiles should handle fine with a single profile — I'll keep the scope description string static rather than varying it per selection, since that's purely informational.

Now I'm starting on validate_plan in verify_results.py, parsing out the selection field into a set of selected names.

Writing selection validation logic... If the selection block is malformed, I append a failure and treat it as if there's no selection (so verification cascades to fail anyway). The expected_roots set should narrow to only packages in the selection when present, and shard assignments should be allowed to be empty if a selection is active rather than treated as an error. The rootCount check already compares against expected_roots, so that stays consistent.

For the shardCount comparison, I need to reorder things since the current check happens before selection is parsed — the expected shard count should be computed from the filtered selected roots rather than the full set. It duplicates some logic to compute selected_heavy_root_count independently inside verify, but that's acceptable since verify is meant to recompute things independently rather than trust the plan.

I realize the cleanest fix is a shared helper that both create_plan and verify call to get the effective shard count from root count and configured setting, avoiding duplicated truth. I'm also considering whether verify should validate that the plan's selected packages match the bundled affected.json decision exactly, which means defining precisely how prepare stores that selection (verbatim after validating against go-list, with fallback to full set) so verify can recompute and compare.

I'm leaning toward only copying affected.json when a narrowed selection is actually applied, so verify's rule becomes simple: if selection exists, affected.json must exist and match; if no selection, there's nothing to check. This adds integrity value since it lets verify trace a narrowed plan back to a recorded decision, though I'm weighing whether this extra check fits the otherwise minimal scope the user wants.

Given the harness's fail-closed design, I'll include it since a selection that can't be authenticated would be inconsistent with the rest of the system. Now I'm updating the windows-test-prepare workflow to deepen the checkout fetch so the PR merge commit's first parent is available for package selection, then adding a new step after Python/Go setup that runs the affected-package selection logic specifically for pull request events.

Writing the pwsh redirection logic, but I need to be careful about PowerShell 7's default encoding behavior for output redirection versus UTF-8 with BOM...

Actually, I should just have the prepare script read with "utf-8-sig" to tolerate any BOM defensively, regardless of the runner's encoding. The `HEAD^1` caret shouldn't need shell escaping in pwsh since it's passed straight through argparse to git.

Adding more arguments to the prepare invocation...

I'm leaving the shard-matrix validation and job names unchanged, since the minimum shard count of one still satisfies the check. Now I'm double-checking whether the required status checks reference each shard job name individually, since the task requires keeping job names exactly as they are.

The per-shard job names like "shard 3" could hang pending if they're required checks but don't run under a reduced matrix — but since the aggregate "windows-test" check is the stable required check, and it evaluates success as long as the needed results succeed, a reduced matrix still resolves fine. For the skip path, I need to write an empty other-events.jsonl file, but verify_other's read_jsonl raises on empty input, so I need to special-case the empty-selection scenario to just confirm the file exists and is empty rather than trying to parse it.

Similarly for shard events, read_jsonl will raise when the stream is empty, so I'm working out logic to allow events=[] when there are no expected assignments and the file is genuinely empty, while still parsing normally if the file has content.

For tests, I'm counting the existing 41 across six files and planning new coverage: verifying that omitting --affected produces a plan identical to passing selected_packages=None, confirming prepare returns None when the flag is absent, and testing that selecting one heavy package filters the plan down to just its roots with an adjusted shard count.

I also want to cover the empty-intersection case (shardCount 1, zero assignments, rootCount 0, still satisfying the workflow matrix invariant), and malformed/invalid affected.json inputs falling back to full mode -- bad JSON, wrong mode, non-list packages, unknown packages, empty lists. I should check whether run_shard's win32 dependency makes it hard to unit test directly, and consider adding selection-aware tests for verify_results too, matching the style of existing test files.
